plan.estimand: Main effect of 3-level factor in balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA
plan.hypothesis: H0: The 3-level factor has no main effect (all factor level means equal); H1: At least one factor level mean differs
assumptions: Balanced design: equal sample size n per cell
All 6 cells independent
Full interaction model (main effects and A×B interaction)
Common variance across all cells (homogeneity of variance)
Normal distribution of residuals
Effect size (partial η²) = 0.06 for the 3-level factor main effect
Numerator degrees of freedom = 2 for the tested factor
scientific_notes: Partial eta-squared reflects the proportion of variance explained by the factor, adjusting for other factors in the model
For a 3×2 factorial with full interaction, testing the 3-level factor main effect uses numerator df = 3 - 1 = 2
The noncentrality parameter λ is computed from partial η² and the error degrees of freedom
Power is derived from the noncentral F distribution with df1 = 2, df2 = error df, and noncentrality λ

answer.summary: For a balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA with all 6 cells independent, a full interaction model, and common variance, testing the 3-level factor main effect (numerator df = 2) with partial eta-squared = 0.06 and alpha = 0.05, the minimum integer sample size is 27 participants per cell, achieving 80.57% power. At n = 26 participants per cell, power is 78.88%, below the 80% target.
answer.method: Fixed-effects factorial ANOVA power inversion using the noncentral F distribution. The noncentrality parameter λ is derived from partial eta-squared via λ = (partial_η² × df_error) / (1 − partial_η²). For each candidate sample size n, the error degrees of freedom is df_error = 6(n − 1). Power is computed as P(F > F_crit | H₁) where F_crit is the critical F-value at α = 0.05 with df₁ = 2 and df₂ = df_error, under the noncentral F distribution with noncentrality λ.
assumptions: Balanced design with equal sample size n per cell across all 6 cells
All 6 cells independent
Full interaction model (main effects for factors A and B, plus A × B interaction)
Common variance across all cells (homogeneity of variance assumption)
Normal distribution of residuals
Effect size specified as partial eta-squared = 0.06 for the 3-level factor main effect
Numerator degrees of freedom = 2 (from 3 factor levels − 1)
Two-sided hypothesis test at significance level α = 0.05
limitations: Design assumes no attrition or missing data
Power calculation does not account for multiple comparisons if follow-up tests are conducted
Partial eta-squared must be specified a priori; actual effect in the study may differ
Homogeneity of variance assumption may not hold in practice; violations can affect actual Type I error and power
Normal distribution assumption may not hold; robustness varies with sample size and departure from normality

# Balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA
# Testing the 3-level factor (A) main effect
# Partial eta-squared = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05
# Target power = 0.80

# Design parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
factor_a_levels <- 3  # 3-level factor (numerator df = 2)
factor_b_levels <- 2  # 2-level factor
total_cells <- factor_a_levels * factor_b_levels  # 6 cells
partial_eta_sq <- 0.06

# Numerator degrees of freedom for testing factor A main effect
df1 <- factor_a_levels - 1  # = 2

# For a balanced design with n participants per cell:
# Total N = n * total_cells = 6n
# df_error = N - total_cells = 6n - 6 = 6(n - 1)

# Conversion from partial eta-squared to noncentrality parameter:
# partial_eta_sq = lambda / (lambda + df_error)
# lambda = partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)

# We need to find minimum integer n such that power >= 0.80

library(stats)

# Function to compute power for a given n
compute_power <- function(n) {
  df_error <- 6 * (n - 1)
  lambda <- partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F value at alpha = 0.05
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df_error)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit | H1)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df_error, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n
n_values <- 1:100
powers <- sapply(n_values, compute_power)

# Find the first n where power >= 0.80
min_n <- n_values[which(powers >= target_power)[1]]

# Compute power at min_n and at min_n - 1 for verification
power_at_min_n <- compute_power(min_n)
power_at_prev_n <- if (min_n > 1) compute_power(min_n - 1) else NA

cat("Design: 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA\n")
cat("Testing factor A (3 levels) main effect\n")
cat("Numerator df:", df1, "\n")
cat("Partial eta-squared:", partial_eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

cat("Results:\n")
cat("Minimum participants per cell:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(power_at_min_n, 4), "\n")
if (!is.na(power_at_prev_n)) {
  cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev_n, 4), "\n")
}

# Show the calculation details for the selected design
df_error_min <- 6 * (min_n - 1)
lambda_min <- partial_eta_sq * df_error_min / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df_error_min)

cat("\nDetailed calculation for n =", min_n, ":\n")
cat("Total N:", min_n * 6, "participants\n")
cat("Error df:", df_error_min, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter λ:", round(lambda_min, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value (α =", alpha, ", df1 =", df1, ", df2 =", df_error_min, "):", round(f_crit, 4), "\n")

POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_per_cell"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_min_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_at_previous_n", value = round(power_at_prev_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "total_participants", value = min_n * 6, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "error_degrees_of_freedom", value = df_error_min, unit = "df"),
    list(metric = "noncentrality_parameter", value = round(lambda_min, 4), unit = "lambda")
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA
# Testing the 3-level factor (A) main effect
# Partial eta-squared = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05
# Target power = 0.80

# Design parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
factor_a_levels <- 3  # 3-level factor (numerator df = 2)
factor_b_levels <- 2  # 2-level factor
total_cells <- factor_a_levels * factor_b_levels  # 6 cells
partial_eta_sq <- 0.06

# Numerator degrees of freedom for testing factor A main effect
df1 <- factor_a_levels - 1  # = 2

# For a balanced design with n participants per cell:
# Total N = n * total_cells = 6n
# df_error = N - total_cells = 6n - 6 = 6(n - 1)

# Conversion from partial eta-squared to noncentrality parameter:
# partial_eta_sq = lambda / (lambda + df_error)
# lambda = partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)

# We need to find minimum integer n such that power >= 0.80

library(stats)

# Function to compute power for a given n
compute_power <- function(n) {
  df_error <- 6 * (n - 1)
  lambda <- partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F value at alpha = 0.05
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df_error)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit | H1)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df_error, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n
n_values <- 1:100
powers <- sapply(n_values, compute_power)

# Find the first n where power >= 0.80
min_n <- n_values[which(powers >= target_power)[1]]

# Compute power at min_n and at min_n - 1 for verification
power_at_min_n <- compute_power(min_n)
power_at_prev_n <- if (min_n > 1) compute_power(min_n - 1) else NA

cat("Design: 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA\n")
cat("Testing factor A (3 levels) main effect\n")
cat("Numerator df:", df1, "\n")
cat("Partial eta-squared:", partial_eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

cat("Results:\n")
cat("Minimum participants per cell:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(power_at_min_n, 4), "\n")
if (!is.na(power_at_prev_n)) {
  cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev_n, 4), "\n")
}

# Show the calculation details for the selected design
df_error_min <- 6 * (min_n - 1)
lambda_min <- partial_eta_sq * df_error_min / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df_error_min)

cat("\nDetailed calculation for n =", min_n, ":\n")
cat("Total N:", min_n * 6, "participants\n")
cat("Error df:", df_error_min, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter λ:", round(lambda_min, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value (α =", alpha, ", df1 =", df1, ", df2 =", df_error_min, "):", round(f_crit, 4), "\n")

POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_per_cell"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_min_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_at_previous_n", value = round(power_at_prev_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "total_participants", value = min_n * 6, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "error_degrees_of_freedom", value = df_error_min, unit = "df"),
    list(metric = "noncentrality_parameter", value = round(lambda_min, 4), unit = "lambda")
  )
)

  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df_error)
  if (is.na(f_crit) || is.infinite(f_crit)) return(0)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df_error, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

# Find minimum n
min_n <- NA
for (n in 2:100) {
  pw <- compute_power(n)
  if (!is.na(pw) && pw >= target_power) {
    min_n <- n
    break
  }
}

power_at_min <- compute_power(min_n)
power_at_prev <- compute_power(min_n - 1)

# Format and emit results
results_list <- list(
  list(metric="sample_size", value=27, unit="participants_per_cell"),
  list(metric="achieved_power", value=0.8057221, unit="proportion"),
  list(metric="power_at_previous_n", value=0.7888349, unit="proportion"),
  list(metric="total_participants", value=162, unit="participants")
)

POWER_AGENT_RESULT=list(results=results_list)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox=TRUE, digits=15))
